title: Natural Remedies / Afterlife Evidence
byline: Coast to Coast AM Staff - October 07, 2026
excerpt: Dr. Randi Shannon discussed holistic health approaches and how we can use natural remedies to support health and manage ailments. Followed by author and grief expert Sandra Champlain with her research into the afterlife.
content:
In the first half, Dr. Randi Shannon of Critical Health News returned to the show to discuss holistic health approaches and how we can use natural remedies to support health and manage ailments alongside modern medicine. Addressing current health concerns, she spoke about the recent pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia and suggested that doxycycline is an effective antibiotic treatment or antidote. She cautioned against fear and media-induced stress, advising people to "stay off all the bad news" and focus on maintaining health rather than anxiety. Touching on the supplement creatine monohydrate, she noted its benefits beyond muscle growth: "It massively supports brain energy, the cognitive function," and aids in muscle preservation especially as people age.

Urging expectant mothers to prioritize nutrition and avoid caffeine and alcohol, she advocated for supplements that provide essential vitamins and minerals to support fetal development. Citing Dr. Wallach's assertion that consistent supplementation could potentially extend life by "an additional 30 years," Shannon shared a compelling case of a severely ill massage therapist who, after six months on a tailored nutrient program, showed remarkable recovery: "Life came back into her face and in her eyes and in her motions."

The conversation also explored Dr. Shannon's diagnostic methods, which include examining the fingernails, and tongue to identify deficiencies and health issues. Responding to a caller's question about stroke recovery, she recommended a natural approach to blood thinning and nutrient replenishment over pharmaceuticals, highlighting the importance of identifying underlying causes of vascular issues. She also announced the publication of her new book, The Language of Spices, which treats spices as medicinal tools rather than just flavorings.

-----------

In the latter half, author and grief expert Sandra Champlain, host of the paranormal podcast Shades of the Afterlife, shared her research into life beyond death and evidence supporting the afterlife. Once a staunch skeptic, she described her journey exploring various phenomena, including mediumship, electronic voice phenomena, hypnosis, and reincarnation, that turned her into a believer. The death of her father intensified her mission to provide comfort to the grieving. She recounted a medium session where a spirit artist produced a drawing of her father as a young man, explaining that spirits pick and choose their best age and memories when they're on the Other Side.

Champlain also discussed her evolving understanding of reincarnation, challenging the idea that souls simply recycle on Earth. She proposed, "We're actually part of a higher soul that remains in the afterlife... a part of them has made a trip back to Earth to explore and learn." Highlighting remarkable cases, she mentioned children with detailed memories of past lives, such as a boy recalling a Hollywood extra's life in the 1940s and another detailing the Titanic's dummy smokestack with precise accuracy.

Referencing cutting-edge paranormal technology, such as the SoulPhone project, she suggested that at a quantum level we are all invisible, vibrating energy, and described how a team of scientific souls on the Other Side were manipulating energy to communicate yes/no responses through mediums. She anticipates this evolving into a full "keyboard" for messages, envisioning a kind of "FaceTime with our loved ones in the afterlife" as a future reality. Champlain rejected the notion that technological communication diminishes the spirit, and said that such devices are "all created under the same umbrella of the light" and are a potential tool for spirits to show that "they're still part of our lives...[and that] we are very much loved."

News segment guest: Harry Dent
